newsitem.title: USA: United Healthcare sees 1996 revs of $10 bln.
newsitem.headline: United Healthcare sees 1996 revs of $10 bln.

text.p: United Healthcare Corp expects revenues this year of about $10 billion, up from $5.9 billion in 1995, said chief operating officer Terry Wills.

In remarks to investors Wednesday at a Robinson-Humphrey conference here, Wills said the largest U.S. managed healthcare company also expects to raise premiums five percent or more on future renewals.
"We have got to make up for a couple of years of inadequate rates," he said.
Wills said the company sees medical-cost inflation running at about 3-4 percent over the short term.

The big jump in sales this year over last year is explained largely by the acqusition of MetraHealth, whose results added to United's revenues only for a portion of 1995's fourth quarter, noted a company spokesman.
Wills told investors that United is pushing through higher premiums, but is not losing business.
"We have not lost significant business as a result of this.... The market is accepting what's going on," he said.
United continues to expect strong growth in 1997, despite higher premiums.

Wills said that most managed care organizations this year set their premium rates too low to cover unexpectedly high increases in medical costs, especially for pharmaceutical products. He said United was no exception to that trend.
"We've had a difficult year operationally," Wills said. "We will work our way out of the situation we've created here."
As for some other HMOs in the sector, Wills said setbacks may not be over. "I think there's still some bloodletting to be done," he said.
The stock was up 1/4 at 37-5/8 in late trade.
